newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish minister says coalition discusses polls.
newsitem.headline: Turkish minister says coalition discusses polls.

text.p: A Turkish cabinet minister said on Tuesday that the two wings of the Islamist-led coalition were discussing elections amid a government crisis over Moslem activism.
"Elections are on the agenda. That is what we are debating," State Minister Salim Ensarioglu told reporters before a planned cabinet meeting.

The possibility of early polls has increasingly been raised since Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's coalition began to buckle under the weight of pressure by the secularist armed forfes for an anti-Islamist crackdown.
"The date is not certain," Ensarioglu said when asked about the timing of any early polls. The next general elections must be held by the year 2000.
Three ministers from Ensarioglu's conservative True Path Party wing of the government have resigned in the last month.
Erbakan and True Path leader Tansu Ciller, the foreign minister, went into a one-to-one meeting at the prime minister's office before the cabinet meeting was due to start.
Ensarioglu denied press reports that Ciller had asked Erbakan to hand over power to her to save the government from collapsing. "We didn't ask for anything like that," he said.
The government needs a simple majority in parliament to call early elections, favoured by some of the opposition.
Four anti-Islamist MPs from the True Path Party quit in recent days, reducing the government's majority on paper to only one, although vacant seats give it a larger margin.
